### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5b6336e1bb6041e2f1918e08a8b99e631586ef1` — the merge of head `f74094ffef8ad7f26c09f19d3abf0842eb2b7b90` into base `eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5b6336e1bb6041e2f1918e08a8b99e631586ef1 && git checkout c5b6336e1bb6041e2f1918e08a8b99e631586ef1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e f74094ffef8ad7f26c09f19d3abf0842eb2b7b90 && git checkout -B drift-repro eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e && git merge --no-ff f74094ffef8ad7f26c09f19d3abf0842eb2b7b90

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eb833b5c4f7ab09c0f86048f34d93dd2fd7ca95e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55837b787f4005ce0ec8179b1e2af73c37f8ddb7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.named-base-overlay-write.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.extension-field-suffix.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.item-name-every-door.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.package-publish-audit-rows.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.recovery-doors-emit-mutation.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.recovery-doors-mutation-projector.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.revert-stored-type-canonical.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.rollback-carries-item-failures.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/29414-commit-revert-own-package-row.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts (`judgeOverrideWrite`, `namedBaseCloseSubject`, `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts (`packagelessCloseSubject`, `classifyPackagelessRow`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts (`restoredBodyWriter`, `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-row-bindings.ts (`resolveOverlayPackageBinding`), packages/metadata-core/src/repository.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts, docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md (D3), docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (D2, D11), skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md

Inputs read: card #29414 (body; comments 6580127079, 6590682952, 6592076882, 6595895198, 6595958400), PR #29797 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs. Check-runs at review time: 13 success, 13 skipped, 20 still in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Live E2E UI, the six Lint jobs, the four Type Check jobs). No derived gate on the head has concluded red; the pending ones are not read as green. The protocol.ts freeze (#27737, 6594835694) is a landing constraint: the design here does not depend on it, and `main` has moved protocol.ts by a small hunk since the merge base, so the seat's delta review after the merge stands as the PR body says.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Plan keyed by the publishing package** (`publishPackageDrafts`, protocol.ts head ~17561): `existedBefore`/`prevVersion` are read from the active row with `package_id: request.packageId`. Right. `listDrafts({ packageId })` filters `package_id` by equality (`packageScopedRowWhere`, sys-metadata-repository.ts ~523–527) and each draft is promoted under `d.packageId`, so the plan now describes the row the promotion writes (ADR-0048's key), and a pair's first publish beside a base-bound row records `existedBefore: false`. The `isMissingTableError` fallback is unchanged.
- **Both revert limbs keyed by the commit's package** (`revertCommit`, head ~19998, ~20141–20165, ~20331–20383): `commitPackageId = row.package_id` (every recorded commit carries one: `recordPackageCommit` takes `packageId: string`); `repo.get`/`repo.delete` on the soft-remove limb and `repo.get`/`repo.restoreVersion` on the restore limb state it. Right as addressing: a pair creation commit beside a base row removes the pair's row and the base row is served again (unit and dogfood cases pin it).
- **Restore binding and the package-less close**: `restorePackageId = current ? commitPackageId : null`; on `null` the restore limb asks `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal(…, 'rollback')` before the #29390 named-base close. `packagelessCloseSubject` answers `null` for any non-empty `packageId` and closes only a `movable` row, so the accept-set change is exactly what the changeset states: a deleted-row restore of a view/dashboard/report/translation/email_template one read-only package ships is refused per item (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, the rollback sentence naming the pair), `success: false`, nothing written; every other restore is as before. Right, as far as it goes — see ④ S1 for the binding chosen when the row is gone.
- **`SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` gains optional `packageId`** (sys-metadata-repository.ts ~1694, ~1753): stated, the active row is resolved under `(org, type, name, package_id)`; omitted, `whereFor(..., undefined)` keeps the any-package resolution. Additive on an exported class; the `MetadataRepository` interface in metadata-core declares no `restoreVersion`, so no published interface widens. Public surface: additive, same idiom as `get`/`delete`. Right.
- **Wire shape**: `RevertPackageCommitResponse.failed[].code` is already optional in `packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`; `rollbackToPackageCommit` reports the refused item per step and continues. No schema change. Right.
- **Commits recorded before this change keep their plan**: nothing rewrites `sys_metadata_commit`. Right as a fact; its consequence on the restore limb is ④ M1.
- **Fixtures**: the seven suites now bind their seeded rows or served commit rows to the commit's package (`PKG`/`app.demo`, `BOUND`); no assertion changes. The publish-audit harness arms its rival write on the second package-scoped read of the name, which is right because the plan read now carries `package_id` and runs before the promotion. The recovery-doors `commitRow` reads `PKG` declared later in the module, at call time, so no TDZ. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; the changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the body carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO migration (the refused revert → the `PUT …?package=base.custom` with the `overrides` declaration), and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (already-registered packageless-overlay-write-closed)`, naming an id that exists at the merge base. Matches AGENTS.md: nothing an author can write changes, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch` with the banner and the disposition kept. The additive `restoreVersion` option does not move the level under the repo's rule (the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone). `Skills-docs: none needed` holds: `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` already says a movable row's package-less save, reset and rollback are refused once movable (D11); nothing it says becomes false. No hand-written page under `content/docs` states the deleted-row revert's behaviour (the drift list is anchor matches on `packageId`/class names). Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, `rollbackMetaItem` shares the addressing defect (class a, measured: `POST /api/v1/meta/view/showcase_task.default/rollback` beside a base-bound row and the pair's override answers 403 naming the base row). Judged: correctly a separate card, not a gap in this narrowing. The per-item door takes no package (`resolveOverlayPackageBinding` reads any package's row by design, protocol-stored-row-bindings.ts), so its fix is a door-surface decision (a `package` selector on the per-item rollback, judged against ADR-0146 D1's "offered only on the writable package"), while the commit doors' address is the commit's own package and this PR completes that. The seat files it; the card's Wanted asked only to measure and say.
- Dev flag, "commits recorded before this change keep their any-package plan … now restores that version into the pair's own row" (carrier: seat, not filed). Not a note: it is a regression this PR introduces on the card's own measured data. Promoted to ④ M1.
- Dev flag, the seed branch's draft read names no package (`repo.get(ref, { state: 'draft' })`, head ~17668). Unmeasured, seed rows have no pair semantics, and the promotion names `d.packageId`; a seat note, not this PR's.
- Addendum item 2 (the spec entry's surface text does not name the commit doors) was ordered out of this PR (`⛔ no packages/spec/**`). Escalated to the seat's spec card as ④ S2; the `already-registered` disposition is mechanically true and the entry's reason already covers the rollback arm by the same sentence.
- Freeze on protocol.ts: a landing constraint, not a finding; the three hunks are pushed before the freeze and the seat runs a delta review after the lift.
- Check-runs pending: the record does not adopt a green it has not seen; the seat re-reads the head's conclusions before the queue.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec on `main`: ADR-0146 D11 closes the package-less write of a movable row at every door and names rollback among them; the registered entry `packageless-overlay-write-closed` says "the package-less save, publish, delete or rollback of a movable one … is refused 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE naming the pair". A commit revert whose restore would insert an unbound row is that write, so refusing it per item makes the spec's own refusal real at a door it had not reached, and nothing a consumer was promised is taken: ADR-0067 D3 promises the pre-commit body, and an unbound row was never the pre-commit state. The addressing half (the plan and both limbs naming the commit's package) delivers what ADR-0048's key and ADR-0067 D3 declare and was simply missing. Trying to break it over the live tree:

- **M1 — must-fix. A legacy pair commit's revert now writes the base's undeclared body into the pair's row, where `main` refused it.** The card's own measured state: a pair (`base.custom`) commit recorded before this change beside a row bound to the read-only base carries `existedBefore: true, prevVersion: N` with N the base row's version (the plan read any package's row). On this head: `current` is the pair's row, so `restorePackageId = commitPackageId` (the pair); the package-less close answers `null` (a package is named) and the named-base close answers `null` (the pair ships nothing); `restoreVersion(ref, N, { packageId: pair })` reads `sys_metadata_history` by `(type, name, version)` with no package (sys-metadata-repository.ts ~1704), which is the base row's body with no `overrides`, and `put`s it into the pair's row. `restoredBodyWriter` (protocol-authoring-gate.ts) asks the name, owner, suffix, extension and save-door families and never the D2 override gate; the repository asks none; the one caller that does is the sibling `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited`, which for a pair-row rollback wraps the writer in `overrideWriteVerdict` and throws `overrideWriteRefusalError` on `refuse` (protocol.ts head ~20776–20790). For the pair writing the base's name with no declaration `judgeOverrideWrite` answers `refuse('undeclared_same_name')` (protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts). So the revert answers `success: true, action: 'restored'`, and the pair's row becomes an undeclared same-name item — the exact shape ADR-0146 D2 says is "refused when undeclared" and the layered read treats as an orphan — and the pair's declaration (`overrides.basedOn` included) is lost. On `main` the same revert is refused by the #29390 close naming the base row (a wrong refusal, but nothing written); this PR turns it into a wrong write. It is a widening on legacy data inside a PR declared `no (narrowing)`, and the dev's report names it as "cannot be told apart". It can: not by the plan, by the body, with the one predicate the sibling already carries. Fix in the restore limb: when `restorePackageId` is the base's pair (`packagedArtifactOwner` + `isCustomizationPairOf`, as the sibling derives `pairRowRollback`), judge the restored body with `overrideWriteVerdict` inside `deriveRestoredBody` and throw the refusal into `failed[]` (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, nothing written) — one predicate, one sentence, no second spelling; the per-item rollback's `intent` derivation for a pair row (`runtime-only`) is the same question and should travel with it. Pin it red-first: serve a commit row for the pair with `existedBefore: true` and the base row's version beside the pair's declared row, and assert `failed[0].code === 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'`, the pair's row unchanged and still declared. The changeset's "Commits recorded before this change keep the plan they recorded … Their revert now restores that version into the pair's own row" then says what the door does: refuses it, naming the declaration.
- **S1 — should-fix. The binding on a gone row.** The commit's package is known, yet when the committing package's row is gone the restore limb hands `null` to both closes and `restoreVersion` writes `activePackageId = null` even with `packageId` stated (sys-metadata-repository.ts ~1757–1770). Two consequences: (a) a pair commit whose pair row was deleted since is refused by the package-less close although restoring into the pair's own row — the pre-commit state ADR-0067 D3 promises, a declared body D2 admits — is open; the changeset's "Now refused" paragraph lists that case. (b) for every type the close does not reach (an object of a writable package) the revert still inserts an unbound row that was never the pre-commit state. If `restoreVersion` wrote the stated `packageId` when no active row is found (`put(..., packageId: opts.packageId ?? activePackageId)`) and the limb passed `commitPackageId` as the binding, the named-base close would be the one question this door asks (a base's gone row is refused there with the same code and the pair-naming sentence), no package-less write would remain for the package-less close to refuse at this door, and the addendum's "exactly as the per-item rollback does" would hold by construction rather than by a shared `null`. The per-item door has no package to state; this door does. Recorded for the seat: it changes the refusal sentence the changeset's TO quotes, so it is a design choice to rule, not a defect that blocks the narrowing.
- **S2 — should-fix, routed.** The registered entry's `surface` names the per-item addresses and the base-named addresses, not `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert` or `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/rollback`, which #29632 and this PR make further addresses of the same close. Text only, `packages/spec`, ordered out of this PR; the seat's spec card carries it (addendum item 2).
- Held: the soft-remove limb under the commit's package writes nothing for a base-bound row and leaves the base served (dogfood case); `rollbackToPackageCommit` reports per item and continues; the `isMissingTableError` branch is unchanged; the plan read's new `package_id` predicate cannot consume the audit harness's one-shot (the harness change says why); `restoreVersion`'s `'packageId' in opts` idiom matches `get` and `delete`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-rooznf`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZUR3xvHyDPCjNL5P4`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7a6e6cd4ef818965c7371b35e54d38f4efbba0c2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.named-base-overlay-write.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/29414-commit-revert-own-package-row.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts (`judgeOverrideWrite`, `namedBaseCloseSubject`, `overrideWriteRefusalError`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commit-record.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-commit.object.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts (`restoredBodyWriter`), docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (D2, D11), docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md (D3), AGENTS.md (the `packages/spec` artifacts table)

Delta review of the FAIL record 6596138372 on `55837b78`. Faces: narrowing (the commit doors) and, new on this head, schema (the `packages/spec` migration entry, by seat claim amendment 6596154325). Inputs: card #29414 with every comment through 6596154325, PR #29797 (body, file list, the net diff against `main` at this head), the delta `55837b78..a8758fbc` and the merge `7a6e6cd4`, the head's check-runs. Check-runs at review time: 14 success, 8 skipped, 19 still in progress (Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1–8, Live E2E UI, six Lint jobs, three Type Check jobs); none concluded red, and the pending ones are not read as green. Everything the earlier record judged and held is unchanged on this head and is not re-judged here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Merge after the split.** `main` at 0e4b0fa4 carries 339f63da (#25467 section 3: four data-write bodies forwarded to `protocol-data-writes.ts`). The PR's net diff against `main` at this head, hunk headers stripped, is byte-identical to the branch's diff against its merge base before the merge (c76c0e04..a8758fbc) on every PR path; `publishPackageDrafts`, `revertCommit`, `restoreWriteFor` and `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited` still live in protocol.ts, and no PR file carries a conflict resolution. Right: the three protocol.ts hunks are re-placed, not re-written.
- **`restoreWriteFor`** (protocol.ts head ~1539–1560): one derivation, now shared by the per-item rollback and the commit revert's restore limb: when `artifactBacked` and the binding is the owner's `.custom` pair (`packagedArtifactOwner` + `isCustomizationPairOf`), intent `runtime-only` and the restored body judged by `overrideWriteVerdict` inside `deriveRestoredBody`, `overrideWriteRefusalError` thrown on `refuse`; otherwise the caller's `artifactBacked` decides the intent and the writer is `restoredBodyWriter` alone. The per-item rollback's behaviour is unchanged by construction (its former inline block is this function with `rollbackPackageId`). Right.
- **Restore binding is always the commit's package** (head ~20120–20160): `restorePackageId = commitPackageId`; the named-base close is asked on it; `repo.restoreVersion(..., { packageId: commitPackageId, intent, deriveRestoredBody })`; the write-through registers under the same package. The package-less close is no longer asked at this door, and it has nothing to judge here: the binding is never `null`. Right — see ③ for the one row that could make it `null`.
- **`restoreVersion` writes the stated package** (sys-metadata-repository.ts ~1765–1770): `packageId: 'packageId' in opts ? (opts.packageId ?? null) : activePackageId`. Stated and the row gone, `put` runs with `parentVersion: null` and creates the package's row again; omitted, the any-package resolution and the unbound fallback as before. The per-item rollback omits it, so it is unchanged. Right.
- **Accept-set on this head**: (a) a restore into a pair row of a version that declares no override is refused per item (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, the save door's `undeclared_same_name` sentence), nothing written; (b) a read-only base's own commit whose base-bound row is gone is refused by the named-base close naming the pair, nothing written (before: an unbound row was inserted); (c) a writable package's or the pair's commit whose row is gone is restored into that package's row (before: an unbound row); (d) everything the pair's or a writable package's row holds restores in place; (e) removals unchanged. Each is pinned: unit cases for (a) the legacy pair plan rewritten onto a real commit row, (b), (c) pair and (c) writable; the dogfood case for (b) asserts the named-base sentence. Right.
- **Spec entry text** (schema face): part (2) of `surface` now names the per-item rollback and the restore of a commit item by `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert` and `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/rollback` as the rollback naming the read-only package, reported per item in `failed[]`; `reason` says the same and that the rest of the commit still reverts. True to the tree: `revertCommit` asks `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal(..., 'rollback')` on `commitPackageId` and reports the item in `failed[]`, and `rollbackToPackageCommit` carries each refused item as one `failed[]` entry (`commitId` + an `error` naming the item) and continues. Part (1), the package-less address, is untouched and the commit doors no longer write that address, so the entry claims nothing false about them. Same `id`, same key; the ADR-0087 registry is projected in memory (AGENTS.md: a migration entry change has nothing to commit), so no generated artifact is owed.
- **Changeset**: title, Clause-② sentence, prose and FROM → TO rewritten to this head's behaviour (the legacy pair commit refused by the gate; the base's gone row refused by the close; the gone row of a writable package or the pair created again under it). The earlier record's M1 wording defect is gone. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the PR body; BREAKING banner, FROM → TO, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered packageless-overlay-write-closed)` naming an id that exists at the merge base. The spec change is text on a registered entry (no authorable key, no new id), so the kind stays `none` and both packages take `patch` under the AGENTS.md rule. The restore into the committing package's row where an unbound row was written before is a changed destination of an existing write and is named in the body under its own heading, not hidden under the narrowing. `Skills-docs: none needed` still holds (SKILL.md: every customization of an installed base lives in its paired `.custom`, declaring `overrides`; a pair row is honoured only when declared). Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Seat rulings 6596154325: M1 fixed, S1 adopted, addendum item 2 landed here as the seat-agreed text amendment, `rollbackMetaItem` filed separately. Each is verified against the tree above; none is taken on the ruling's word.
